'''Rastislav Káčer''' (born 9 July 1965)<ref>{{Citation |title=Rastislav Káčer: Náš vzťah je karmický |url=https://www.thebusinesssoiree.com/clanek/rastislav-kacer-nas-vztah-je-karmicky |language=cs |issn=2336-7296}}</ref> is a [[Slovakia|Slovak]] diplomat, former ambassador of [[Slovakia]] to US, [[Hungary]] and the [[Czech Republic]]. From September 2022 to May 2023, Káčer served as the [[Minister of Foreign Affairs (Slovakia)|Minister of Foreign and European Affairs]] of Slovakia.

== Early years ==
Káčer self-declared himself as a three-quarter [[Slovaks|Slovak]] and quarter [[Hungarians|Hungarian]] with familial origin from [[Tekov]] region.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Káčer |first1=Rastislav |author1-link=Rastislav Káčer |title=MÝTY V NÁS A OKOLO NÁS |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=A2jq3YIRK40&t=389s |website=YouTube |publisher=Nadácia Polis |language=sk |format=video |date=25 April 2023}}</ref> Káčer studied primary and secondary schools in [[Žarnovica]] and [[Nitra]]. After graduating high school, he was unable to study Medicine due to his opposition to the Communist regime.  After working in a factory for a year, he managed to enroll at the [[Slovak University of Technology in Bratislava]] to study [[Chemistry]]. After graduating in 1989, he worked for two years as a Researcher in an Agricultural research institute in [[Nitra]].<ref name="Vojtenyiova">{{Citation |last=Vojtényová |first=Denisa |title=R. Káčer: Fascinujúce je ovplyvňovať chod štátu |date=23 July 2003 |url=https://hnonline.sk/hnporadna/moja-kariera/64058-r-kacer-fascinujuce-je-ovplyvnovat-chod-statu |language=sk}}</ref> Following the [[Velvet Revolution]], Káčer studied [[International relations]] at the [[Comenius University]], graduating in 1995.

== Career in diplomacy ==
Káčer has been employed at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs since 1992. Between 1994 and 1998, he served as the first Secretary of Slovak delegation to [[NATO]].  Between 2001 and 2003 he served as the State Secretary at the Defense ministry responsible from admission negatiotions with [[NATO]].<ref name="Globsec">{{Citation |title=Rastislav Káčer's profile at the Globsec website |url=https://www.globsec.org/people/rastislav-kacer/ |access-date=3 October 2022 |archive-date=7 October 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221007091539/https://www.globsec.org/people/rastislav-kacer |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Between 2003 and 2008 Káčer served as the Slovakia's ambassador in the United States. After the end of his tenure, he co-founded the influential Slovak think tank [[GLOBSEC]].<ref name="Globsec" /> Between 2013 and 2018 he served as the ambassador to [[Hungary]]. His decision to join over 30 countries that displayed the [[rainbow flag]] on their embassy buildings in [[Budapest]] to support the [[pride parade]] was criticized by anti-LGBT activists in Slovakia.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Takáč |first=Adam |title=Lajčák zahriakol Káčera za dúhovú vlajku |url=https://www.postoj.sk/15890/lajcak-zahriakol-kacera-za-duhovu-vlajku |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=Postoj.sk |language=sk}}</ref>

Between 2018 and 2020 Káčer served as the ambassador in [[Czech Republic]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Cibulka |first1=Ľubor |last2=Domin |first2=Marek |date=3 September 2018 |title=Formovanie ústavného postavenia prezidenta Slovenskej republiky (Približovanie alebo vzďaľovanie sa modelu z prvej československej republiky) |journal=AUC Iuridica |volume=2018 |issue=3 |pages=49–70 |doi=10.14712/23366478.2018.18 |s2cid=187383306 |issn=2336-6478|doi-access=free }}</ref>

== Foreign minister ==
Following the departure of the [[Freedom and Solidarity]] party from the government coalition, Káčer was asked by the Defense Minister [[Jaroslav Naď]] with the blessing of Prime Minister [[Eduard Heger]] to replace the [[Freedom and Solidarity]] nominee [[Ivan Korčok]] as the Foreign minister.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kern |first=Miro |date=6 September 2022 |title=Kandidátmi na ministrov sú veľvyslanec Káčer, sudca Bradáč aj Daniel Bútora |url=https://dennikn.sk/2998356/kandidatmi-na-ministrov-su-velvyslanec-kacer-sudca-bradac-aj-daniel-butora/ |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=Denník N |language=sk}}</ref> Káčer accepted to facilitate continuation of pro-Western and pro-European foreign policy of his predecessor, including crucially the support for Ukraine in the [[Russo-Ukrainian War]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=13 September 2022 |title=R. Káčer: Post šéfa diplomacie nesie mnoho rizík |url=https://www.teraz.sk/slovensko/r-kacer-post-sefa-diplomacie-nesie/660203-clanok.html |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=TERAZ.sk |language=sk}}</ref>

== Political views ==
Káčer is strongly supportive of Slovakia's pro-Western orientation and denounced the pro-Russian views of Prime Minister [[Robert Fico]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=11 September 2022 |title=Káčer chcel byť ešte šťastný muž v domácnosti. Bude šéf diplomacie |url=https://spravy.pravda.sk/domace/clanok/639907-kacer-chcel-byt-este-stastny-muz-v-domacnosti-bude-sef-diplomacie/ |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=Pravda.sk |language=sk}}</ref> He is a staunch critic of former Hungarian Prime Minister [[Viktor Orbán]] and Russian president [[Vladimir Putin]].<ref name=":0" /> He strongly supports arms transfers to Ukraine, including the transfer of Slovakia's [[S-300 missile system]] to aid Ukraine's defenders. He also strongly supports [[International sanctions during the Russian invasion of Ukraine|international sanctions]] against Russia to remain in place for as long as Russia keeps occupying Ukraine's territory including [[Crimea]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Káčer |first=Rastislav |date=9 April 2022 |title=Rastislav Káčer: Videli sme deň vzopnutia |url=https://www.tyzden.sk/komentare/83658/rastislav-kacer-videli-sme-den-vzopnutia/ |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=.týždeň|language=sk}}</ref>

Káčer considers himself a [[Liberal conservatism|liberal conservative]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Kern |first=Miro |date=30 July 2020 |title=Weiss po siedmich rokoch skončí ako veľvyslanec v Prahe, nahradí ho Káčer |url=https://dennikn.sk/1986761/weiss-po-siedmich-rokoch-skonci-ako-velvyslanec-v-prahe-nahradi-ho-kacer/ |access-date=2022-10-03 |website=Denník N |language=sk}}</ref> In 2023, Káčer briefly served as a deputy chairman of the [[Democrats (Slovakia)|Democrats]] party, but decided to leave politics in May 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2023-05-09 |title=Rastislav Káčer opúšťa Hegerovu stranu. Je z nej sklamaný |url=https://www.startitup.sk/rastislav-kacer-opusta-hegerovu-stranu-je-z-nej-sklamany/ |access-date=2023-06-08 |website=Startitup.sk |language=sk}}</ref>
